name: Ethernet board display
look: a desk device with a wide screen on the left and a round touch button on the right
picture_prompt: Product concept render of a small 3D-printable desk device, seen from the front and slightly to one side. It is wider than it is tall. One smooth continuous body with soft rounded corners. On the left of the front is a flat wide rectangular screen, about 55 mm wide and 27 mm tall. On the right is one shallow round dimple about 12 mm across, used as a touch button, with no knobs. One matte plastic colour with a dark screen. Soft studio light, plain light background. Flat bottom, flat back, no text, no logos, no speaker holes, no feet, no visible seams, no cables.
sheet: Front faces -y and stands upright. World +z is up.
Left about 70% of the front: the screen, landscape, a separate board just behind the front wall.
Right part of the front: the touch sensor, flat behind the front wall, reached through a round opening in a shallow dimple. Its pins point into the case, toward +y.
The controller is a separate board behind the screen, so its USB reaches the left wall. Its top faces the back (+y) and its pins point forward (-y), with their plugs between it and the screen.
USB opens on the left side (-x).
The wires run behind the screen board as one neat bundle, side by side, and do not show from outside.
The seam is a flat plane near the back, so from the front the Shell looks like one continuous body and the Base is only a rear cover.
The controller sits on a holder built into the rear cover. The rear cover is a flat plate with holder and stops on it, and it closes from +y.
